meta.name: Daily Cooking
meta.note: All recipes are vegetarian with eggs allowed. Amounts are as written on Vismai Food, treated as one household batch for 2 people. The shopping list scales amounts by servings / 2. Ingredients marked approx use a sensible standard amount where the site gave no exact quantity. Poppy seeds are restricted in Canada, so recipes that list them carry a note to skip them or use roasted Bengal gram instead. The Daily Cooking Space returned 31 recipes in getstate, not 32 as its seed text states, so the base count here is 31.

recipes.name: Aloo Capsicum Curry
recipes.note: Uses a blender/mixie for the peanut-tomato paste.
steps: Fry the peanuts; add onion and chilli till soft.
Add tomato, salt and turmeric; cook with the lid on till soft.
Grind to a smooth paste.
Fry the potato pieces on a low flame, lidded, till golden.
Add capsicum and onion; fry 2-3 min.
Add the paste, water and chilli powder; cook 7-8 min.
Add garam masala and coriander; cook 2-3 min.

recipes.name: Aloo Rice (Potato Rice)
recipes.note: Uses a blender/mixie for the mint-coriander paste.
steps: Grind mint, coriander, garlic, ginger, chilli, curd and lemon into a paste.
Fry the potato pieces in oil.
Add onion, curry leaves, tomato, cumin and chilli powders.
Add the cooked rice and the green paste.
Toss on a high flame so the flavours stick.
Serve with cool raita.

recipes.name: Bendakaya Pulusu (Okra Tamarind Gravy)
steps: Temper the seeds, dals, garlic and curry leaves till the fenugreek turns golden.
Fry the onion and green chillies.
Add turmeric and okra; fry 5 min till red spots appear.
Add tamarind juice, salt and jaggery; cover and cook till the okra is soft.
Stir in the besan-water and cook 3-4 min to thicken.

recipes.name: Bhindi do Pyaza (Okra Onion Curry)
steps: Wash and wipe the okra fully dry; cut with a dry knife.
Fry the okra covered on a high flame till the edges colour, this removes the stickiness.
Fry the onion petals till just pink.
Add the tomato paste and diced tomato with the spices.
Combine the okra, onion and tomato masala.
Garnish with coriander; serve with roti or rice.

recipes.name: Carrot Rice
steps: Have fluffy, salted cooked rice ready.
Temper the whole spices and cashews in oil.
Fry the onion and chillies.
Add grated carrot and sambar powder; fry briefly.
Toss in the cooked rice, lemon juice and coriander; mix well.
Serve for a lunch box or with raita.

recipes.name: Cheese Bread Omelette
steps: Beat the eggs well with onion, tomato, capsicum, chillies and spices.
Toast the bread slices in butter on both sides.
Pour the egg into the pan; while half-cooked, place toast and cheese on top so they stick.
Cook till about 90% done, then fold.
Rest 10-15 seconds and serve with tomato sauce.

recipes.name: Chocolate Oats
steps: Roast the dry coconut and set aside.
Boil the milk and water.
Mix the cocoa into a little hot milk till lump-free.
Cook the oats in the milk till soft; add the cocoa mix and cook 2-3 min (do not over-thicken).
Off the heat, add vanilla, a pinch of salt and honey.
Serve hot topped with coconut, banana, almonds and dates.

recipes.name: Coconut Rice
recipes.note: The recipe page lists 1 3/4 liter coconut milk, but the site's own tip says 1 3/4 cup per cup of rice, so use the cup measure.
steps: Pressure-cook the rice in coconut milk and water (2 whistles on medium, 1 on high).
Add salt while the rice is still hot; mix.
Temper cashews, dals and spices; fry the grated coconut 30 sec.
Mix the tempering into the rice, sprinkle coriander and serve.

recipes.name: Crispy Aloo Fry
steps: Peel and cut the potatoes evenly; wash 3-4 times.
Soak at least 15 min to remove starch.
Parboil lightly (water just bubbling at the edges), then drain.
Dry-roast urad dal, chillies and cumin; grind to a spice powder.
Temper mustard, cumin, garlic, hing and curry leaves.
Fry the potato till crisp outside and soft inside; toss with the spice powder and salt.

recipes.name: Dal Khichdi (Restaurant Style)
recipes.note: Two tadkas and a 1-hour soak make it the most involved rice dish here, pick a day with time.
steps: Soak the dal and rice for at least 1 hr; wash.
Pressure-cook with water to a soft, mushy consistency (add water in 2 steps).
Make an onion-tomato-garlic-ginger tadka with the spices.
Combine the khichdi with the tadka; thin with hot water so it stays soft as it cools.
Finish with a second ghee tadka; serve hot.

recipes.name: Easy Egg Pulao
steps: Temper the whole spices in ghee.
Fry the onion till golden.
Add ginger-garlic, chillies and the spice powders; fry.
Fry the boiled eggs till golden on top.
Add the cooked rice, coriander and mint; toss on a high flame.
recipes.timeLabel: ~20 min + cooked rice and boiled eggs

recipes.name: Egg Fried Rice (Restaurant Style)
recipes.note: The recipe's Aromatic Powder is a specialty Indo-Chinese seasoning that is hard to find in Toronto, the site says it can be dropped entirely, so leave it out.
steps: Have fluffy cooked rice ready (cook to 90%, drain, cool).
Stir-fry the thin-cut vegetables on a high flame to about 60%, keep them crunchy.
Scramble the eggs in the same pan.
Add rice, soya sauce, vinegar, pepper and a pinch of sugar.
Toss on a high flame; add spring onion; serve with ketchup or Manchuria.
recipes.timeLabel: 5 min once veg is chopped, + cooked rice

recipes.name: Egg Masala Fry (Guntur Style)
recipes.note: The site lists poppy seeds, which are restricted in Canada, the site itself says to use cashew nuts instead, so this list uses cashews.
steps: Roast all the spice-powder ingredients on a low flame till aromatic.
Grind to a powder.
Fry the boiled eggs covered till golden.
In the same oil, soften the onion and chillies with salt.
Add turmeric, mirchi and ginger-garlic paste; fry 2 min.
Add the egg pieces and spice powder; cook 2 min; sprinkle mint and coriander.

recipes.name: Godhuma Rava Upma
steps: Warm-roast the rava without browning it; set aside.
Fry cashews and chana dal golden.
Temper mustard and cumin, then ginger, chilli and curry leaves.
Fry the onion, then the carrot.
Add hot water and salt, bring to a boil; add rava gradually, stirring.
Cover and cook on low till soft and fluffy.
Add ghee and coriander; serve hot.

recipes.name: Instant Spongy Idli
recipes.note: Needs an idli stand / steamer. If you do not have one, swap this for Rava Adai.
steps: Soak the poha in buttermilk till soft and paste-like (grind if needed).
Mix with fine rice rava, soda and salt into a batter.
Pour into a greased idli stand.
Steam in boiling water: 5 min on high, then 2 min on low.
Rest 2 min off the heat, then remove the idlis.
Serve hot with sambar or chutney.

recipes.name: Miriyala Pappu Charu (Pepper Dal Rasam)
steps: Pressure-cook the soaked dal with turmeric (4 whistles); mash.
Dry-roast the pepper-masala spices till the pepper splutters; grind semi-coarse.
Make a ghee tadka.
Saute the onion till translucent and the tomato till soft.
Add tamarind and salt; boil; add the pepper masala.
Add the mashed dal and 1 litre water; simmer 20 min.
Add coriander; serve hot with rice or pongal.

recipes.name: Oats Upma
steps: Warm-roast the oats on a low flame and set aside.
Fry the cashews golden and remove.
Temper mustard and cumin, then add ginger and curry leaves.
Soften the onion and chillies.
Fry carrot and beans covered, then add peas.
Add hot water and bring to a rolling boil.
Add oats little by little, stirring to avoid lumps; cook covered 7-8 min.
Finish with coriander, coconut and lemon; top with cashews; serve hot.

recipes.name: Onion Kurma
recipes.note: Uses a blender/mixie for the onion-coconut-cashew paste.
steps: Fry onion, coconut, cashews and sesame; grind to a paste.
Fry the ginger-garlic and spice powders in oil.
Add the tomato paste and the big onion pieces.
Add the tamarind pulp.
Stir in the onion paste; simmer till thick.
Garnish with coriander; serve with chapati or roti.

recipes.name: Paneer Butter Masala
recipes.note: Uses a blender/mixie for the tomato-cashew gravy.
steps: Boil the diced tomato, onion, spices and cashews in water.
Grind to a smooth paste.
Melt butter with oil, fry the Kashmiri chilli, add the paste; cook till thick.
Add kasuri methi, cumin and coriander powders, salt, sugar and water; boil.
Skim off the frothy layer.
Add the paneer and cook 2-3 min.
Add the cream and mix.
Sprinkle coriander; serve with roti or rice.

recipes.name: Peanut Spicy Rice
recipes.note: Uses a blender/mixie for the peanut powder.
steps: Roast the peanuts 3-4 min on a low flame.
Roast the red chillies, coconut and sesame one by one till aromatic.
Cool and grind to a coarse powder.
Heat oil and temper mustard, dals and curry leaves; add cooked rice, salt and the peanut powder; mix.
Let it cool before packing.
recipes.timeLabel: Prep 2 min, Cook 15 min, Total 17 min, Serves 4 (site-stated)

recipes.name: Perfect Rava Upma
steps: Roast rava with cumin on a low flame about 10 min till aromatic.
Temper mustard and dals, then curry leaves, cashews, chillies and ginger.
Boil the water and milk together.
Add salt to the rava, pour rava slowly into the boiling liquid, stirring.
Cook 5 min, then rest 5 min.
Add ghee, mix and serve.

recipes.name: Potato Curry (Street Food Style)
steps: Boil the potatoes and mash (mash some fully, that thickens the curry).
Temper the whole spices in oil.
Fry onion, tomato and ginger-garlic with the powdered spices.
Add the mashed potato and water.
Simmer on a slow fire so the potato absorbs the spices.
Finish with coriander and kasuri methi.

recipes.name: Potato Peas Rice (Aloo Matar Pulao)
steps: Soak the basmati for 1 hr.
Temper the whole spices and onion in the cooker.
Add ginger-garlic, potato, peas, rice, water, salt and herbs.
Pressure-cook for 2 whistles.
Rest till the steam releases; fluff and serve.

recipes.name: Pudina Rice (Mint Rice Pulao)
steps: Fry the whole spices in oil and ghee.
Fry onion and chillies till golden.
Add salt, garam masala and ginger-garlic paste; cook 1 min.
Add the mint paste and fry till the oil separates; add mint leaves for 1 min.
Add the cooked rice and mix well.
Add lemon juice if you like; garnish with mint or fried onion; serve with raita.

recipes.name: Rava Adai
steps: Mix rava, rice flour, curds, water, salt and vegetables into a thick batter.
Rest about 30 min (do not over-ferment or it loses its crunch).
Rub the pan with an onion slice so the adai does not stick.
Spread the batter thick by tapping, not thin like a dosa.
Cook till crisp outside and soft inside.
Serve with chutney, sambar or jaggery.
recipes.timeLabel: Batter ready in 30 min; ~15 min cooking

recipes.name: Semiya Curd Bath
steps: Boil water, add vermicelli for 30 sec-1 min, then drain.
Rinse with cold water and cool completely.
Fry the cashews and set aside.
Temper the spices with curry leaves, chilli and ginger.
Whisk the curd with cucumber and salt.
Add the cooled vermicelli, tempering, pepper, pomegranate, cashews and coriander; mix.
Serve cool (stir in a little boiled, cooled milk if it turns lumpy).

ingredients.d: Eggs (1 per serving, 2 each for 2 people)

recipes.name: Spicy Indian Shakshuka
steps: Temper the cumin; fry garlic and onion till pink.
Add the capsicums, cover and cook 3 min.
Add the tomatoes; cook 7-8 min till soft.
Add the spice powders and hot water; cook 4-5 min till mushy; add garam masala if using.
Make wells in the sauce and crack an egg into each.
Cover till the eggs are firm.
Garnish with coriander; serve with rice or roti.

recipes.name: Sweet Corn Coconut Milk Kichidi
steps: Boil the corn till 80% done; grind most of it to a coarse paste.
Temper chilli, cumin, garlic, green chilli and ginger.
Saute the corn paste 3 min with a little water.
Add the soaked rice for 2 min, then the coconut milk.
Add water and pressure-cook for 3 whistles.
Adjust with hot water, mash and saute 4-5 min.
Stir in ghee; serve hot.

recipes.name: Telangana Style Masala Egg Curry
recipes.note: Uses a blender/mixie for the gravy paste.
steps: Roast the groundnuts and fenugreek on a low flame.
Add coriander and cumin, then sesame, then coconut; roast; grind to a powder.
Fry the onions well; add them to the powder.
Grind to a smooth paste with ginger-garlic, mirchi, salt, tamarind and turmeric.
Slit the boiled eggs; fry on a high flame.
Fry the paste till the oil separates.
Add water and cook; add the eggs and cover for 15 min.
Garnish with coriander.

recipes.name: Tomato Bath
steps: Roast the rava on a low flame till aromatic.
Roast the cashews in ghee and oil.
Temper the dals and seeds; fry the onion 2 min.
Add chilli and ginger; cook till the onion softens.
Add tomato for 2 min, then carrot, peas, turmeric, curry leaves and salt; cook the veg to about 80%.
Add water, bring to a boil, add rava and cover for 3 min.
Add coriander, cashews and ghee; serve.

recipes.name: Tomato Egg Drop Curry
steps: Temper mustard and cumin; fry the onion.
Add tomatoes, ginger-garlic and spices; cook to a gravy, add water and boil.
Break the eggs directly into the boiling gravy in different spots.
Cook about 10 min till the eggs set and absorb the masala.
Add pepper and coriander; serve with rice.

ingredients.d: Green coriander with stalks, a small bunch
2 tbsp tamarind (extracted from a marble-size tamarind)

recipes.name: Tomato Rasam
recipes.note: Mash the tomatoes by hand with the coriander stalks, do not grind the skin in a mixie.
steps: Add the green coriander stalks to the tomatoes and squeeze hard and remove the juice. Remove the remaining pulp and add 1/2 litre of water to the paste.
Pound cumin seeds, pepper, garlic and curry leaves to a coarse paste.
Pour the tomato rasam into a vessel and add green chillies. Cover and cook until the green chillies soften.
Once green chillies are cooked, add the cumin-pepper paste, turmeric and salt and boil once on medium flame and switch off the stove.
Heat oil for the seasoning and add mustard seeds. Let them splutter and add the rest of the ingredients and mix in the rasam. Eat happily with hot rice.

recipes.name: Rice Rava Upma (Uppudu Pindi)
recipes.note: Make the rice rava first by grinding rice with pepper, red gram and cumin, then cook it like upma. One cup rava needs 3 cups water.
steps: Wash the rice and strain. While it is still damp, add pepper, red gram, cumin seeds and dry in a thin layer in the shade.
An hour later, when the rice is dry, add to a mixie and run the pulse and grind to a coarse rava.
Heat oil in a thick-bottomed vessel and add mustard seeds, black gram, Bengal gram and roast.
Add red chilli and curry leaves.
Add boiling water and salt, raw coconut and let the water boil on high flame.
While the water is boiling, add rice semolina, mix well, cover and cook until soft. Keep mixing from the bottom.
Add 1 tbsp of ghee, mix and remove from fire. It tastes terrific while hot and accompanied by mango pickles.

recipes.name: Moong Dal Sambar (Pesarapappu Pulusu)
recipes.note: No tamarind in this sambar, it uses lemon juice instead. Serve with hot rice and ghee, idli or dosa.
steps: Roast the split green gram on a low flame until it gives out a pleasant aroma. Then wash and cook to a soft paste in 2.5 cups of water.
In a vessel, add onions, green chillies, turmeric, salt and water and cook until the onions are cooked soft.
Add the cooked split green gram into the onions and mix well. Let the sambar cook for 3-4 minutes. (If it seems too thick, you could add some water)
In the boiling rasam, add some lemon juice and switch off the stove.
Add the ingredients for seasoning one by one into the sambar and mix well. Add chopped green coriander at last.
This split green gram sambar is delicious when eaten with rice, idly, or dosa.

ingredients.d: 300 g tender ivy gourd pieces (long, thin sliced)
Water, sufficient to immerse the vegetable pieces

recipes.name: Tindora Curry (Dondakaya Curry)
recipes.note: No onion or garlic in this recipe, the site says they do not go well with it.
steps: Put the long, thin sliced pieces of tender ivy gourd, add salt and turmeric and pour water enough to immerse the pieces. Cook to one whistle on a high flame and remove.
Add the ingredients for coconut spice one by one to the pan. Start with mustard seeds and add raw coconut at the end and fry. Once it is cool, grind the mixture into a powder.
Heat oil, add mustard seeds, curry leaves and fry.
Add the coarse coconut spice powder, add tamarind juice and cook until the oil separates.
Once the oil separates, add the cooked ivy gourd pieces, straining the water, and cook slowly in tamarind juice for 4-5 minutes.
Add some jaggery, mix and remove.

recipes.name: Vangi Bath Curry (Brinjal Fry)
recipes.note: Poppy seeds are restricted in Canada, skip them or use roasted Bengal gram instead. The spice powder keeps fresh for a week in an airtight container.
steps: For the masala, melt ghee first and roast black gram and Bengal gram, stirring all the time.

While they are changing colour, add all other ingredients and roast on low flame until the colour looks good and it smells nice. Remove from fire, let it cool. Add jaggery and grind it into a soft powder in a mixie.
Heat oil, add curry leaves and fry. Add brinjal pieces and turmeric and mix well. Cover it and let the pieces cook well on medium flame.
Once the brinjal pieces are cooked well, add tamarind paste and salt. Cover it and let it cook until the vegetable absorbs the paste.
Then add the powder, mix well and fry for another two minutes.
Add 2 tsp ghee and mix well and remove from fire.
This tastes very good with hot rice with ghee.

recipes.name: Brinjal Fenugreek Fry (Brinjal Methi Fry)
recipes.note: Brinjal needs adequate oil to taste good, the site says you can cook it with less oil too, but it does not turn out so tasty.
steps: Heat oil and add brinjal, sliced into two-inch pieces and let them cook to 80 percent until they change color. Set them aside.
Add mustard seeds, cumin seeds, asafoetida, chopped ginger and garlic, and fry.
Add the chopped onions, let them turn soft, and then add tomatoes and green chillies and cook until the tomatoes turn soft.
Add turmeric, coriander powder, salt and mirchi powder.
Finely chop the fenugreek leaves, add it to the mixture and cook until oil separates.
Once the leaves are cooked, add the brinjal pieces, let them cook for another 3 minutes and remove from fire.

recipes.name: Chilli Paneer Gravy
recipes.note: A thick, tasty accompaniment for fried rice, done in about 10 minutes. If aromatic powder is not available, skip it.
steps: Add maida, corn flour, salt and pepper powder and mix well. Add paneer cubes and coat them well with a spoon.
Add some water and mix with a spoon or rotate the vessel until the flour sticks to the cubes.
Fry paneer cubes on medium flame until they turn light golden and the flour coating turns crisp. Set aside.
Heat oil in a pan and add ginger garlic paste, green chillies and onion and fry until the onions turn soft.
Now add onions, capsicum strings, green chilli pieces and cook on high flame for 2-3 minutes.
Then add the remaining sauces, powders and fry on high flame until the oil separates.
When the oil separates, add 300 ml water and boil it on high flame. After 2-3 minutes, add paneer pieces and let cook for 2 minutes.
In the simmering gravy, add 1 tbsp of corn flour mixed in 3 tbsp of water and let it boil for 2 minutes on high flame until it turns thick.
When the gravy is thick, add the inch-long spring onion pieces and let boil for another minute. Then sprinkle the chopped spring onions and remove from the fire and serve.

recipes.name: Schezwan Veg Fried Rice
recipes.note: Soak a cup of basmati rice for an hour, cook to 80% and cool, so the rice stays fluffy. If aromatic powder is not available, skip it.
steps: Heat the oil and add dry red chilies, grated carrots, chopped beans and fry to 70 percent on high flame.
Add schezwan sauce and fry further.
Add salt, white pepper powder, aromatic powder, star anise powder and mix well.
Add the fluffy rice and toss on a high flame.
Now add light soya sauce and vinegar and toss well on a high flame.
Sprinkle a little sugar and chopped spring onions, toss well and remove from fire.

ingredients.d: 1 cup basmati rice (soaked for an hour)

recipes.name: Khuska Pulao
recipes.note: Soak the rice for 1 hour first, or the khuska turns into a soft lump. Serve with raita or a masala curry.
steps: Melt ghee in a pressure cooker and add cardamoms, cloves, cinnamon, star anise, nutmeg and biryani leaf and fry.
Add cumin seeds and saunf. Then add onions and green chillies and fry well.
Fry ginger garlic paste and add diced ripe tomatoes, turmeric, salt, mirchi powder, garam masala and cook slowly until the tomatoes turn into a pulp.
Add 1/2 cup non-sour whisked curds and mix well and cook until the ghee comes to the surface.

When the ghee comes to the surface, add coriander and mint leaves and mix well. Then add the basmati rice, soaked for an hour in water, and blend on high flame for a minute, taking care to see that the grain does not break.
Add one cup of water, let the rice cook on high flame till one whistle, switch off and leave it for 20 minutes.
After 20 minutes, take the lid off and turn over the rice from the bottom with a flat spoon. And fragrant khuska is ready.
Khuska can be eaten with raita, masala curry or with any non-veg curry.
recipes.timeLabel: Not stated on site, + 1 hr rice soak

recipes.name: Tamarind Rice (Prasadam Pulihora)
recipes.note: Temple-style tamarind rice. Sesame oil or groundnut oil tastes best here.
steps: Soak tamarind in hot water and extract 250 ml of tamarind juice.
Wash rice and cook with two cups of water per cup of rice on three whistles.
When the steam goes out of the rice, add turmeric, oil, green chillies, curry leaves and salt while the rice is still hot.
Grind mustard seeds, red chillies, ginger and a little salt to a soft paste.
Heat 2 tsp of oil and roast mustard seeds and fenugreek seeds. Add curry leaves.
Pour the tamarind extract and add grated jaggery and cook until it becomes a thick paste.
Once it is thick, add the mustard seeds paste and let it cook. After it is thoroughly cooked, switch off the stove, let it cool completely and then mix it well in the rice.
For the second seasoning, heat 1/4 cup oil, add mustard and let them crackle. Then add groundnuts, Bengal gram and black gram and roast them.
Add red chillies and curry leaves and fry them and add to the rice. And your prasadam pulihora is ready.

recipes.name: Dhaba Style Spicy Okra (Bhindi Masala)
recipes.note: Never add water to this curry, everything cooks in oil only. If it seems absolutely necessary, add 1 tbsp of water when you fry the spices.
steps: Heat 2 tbsp oil and add okra pieces and fry till they turn dark. Set aside.
In the same pan, add 3 tbsp of oil and roast cumin and mustard seeds.
Add thinly chopped onions and fry till they turn light golden. While the onions are changing color, add curry leaves.
When onions change color, add ginger garlic paste, rest of the spices, salt, mirchi powder, garam masala, coriander powder, cumin powder, and others and fry till oil separates.
Add tomato paste and cook until oil separates.
After the oil rises to the surface, add the bhindi pieces and let it cook for 3-4 minutes. Remove from fire when oil separates.
This bhindi masala curry goes well with rice and rotis.

ingredients.d: 250 g onions, sliced into long pieces

recipes.name: Hotel Style Puri Curry (Poori Masala)
recipes.note: Slice the onions into long pieces, do not chop them finely, or they mix into the curry. The boiled potato and the lemon juice are both optional.
steps: Heat oil in a pan and add mustard seeds, Bengal gram, black gram, cumin seeds, red chillies, curry leaves one after the other and fry.
Add sliced green chillies, sliced onions and turmeric and fry the onions on a high flame for 3 minutes.
Add 1/2 litre of water and salt, cover it and cook until the onions turn soft.
Gradually add Bengal gram flour mixed in water to a thin consistency without lumps and mix it well. Add chopped ginger and mix.
Once the Bengal gram flour gets mixed in the curry, smash a boiled potato and add it to the curry.
After cooking for 2 minutes, switch off the stove, add lemon juice and remove it from the fire.

ingredients.d: 2 tsp oil (to cook and to sprinkle on noodles after cooking)

recipes.name: Chilli Garlic Veg Noodles
recipes.note: Cook the noodles only to 80%, or they turn into a tangled, broken mess when you toss them. If aromatic powder is not available, skip it.
steps: Pour water into a vessel, add salt and oil, let the water boil. Add the noodles to the boiling water and cook on a high flame to 80%.
Drain the water off the cooked noodles and spread on a plate. Sprinkle oil and move them without breaking the noodles and let it cool.
Heat oil in a pan and add garlic, ripe red chillies, dry chillies and fry.
In the fried garlic, add onions, three colors of capsicum, and toss for 2-3 minutes on a high flame so that they are cooked to 60%.
Add the cooled noodles to the pan and add the rest and toss on a high flame for 2-3 minutes.
Before you remove from the fire, add vinegar, water, and spring onion, toss for another minute.
Serve it hot with veg manchuria or tomato ketchup.
recipes.timeLabel: ~10 min once ingredients are at hand

recipes.name: Okra Garlic Fry (Lehsuni Bhindi)
recipes.note: Wash and air-dry the okra, then cut into inch-long pieces, or it turns sticky. This fry stays fresh for at least 3 days.
steps: Heat oil and add inch-long okra pieces and fry till golden. (Not too golden, as if they are too crispy they become bitter when they cool down)
Add garlic, cumin seeds, salt and mirchi powder and grind to a coarse mixture and mix in the hot, fried okra pieces.
In the same oil in which the okra pieces were fried, add peanuts and curry leaves and mix it in the okra pieces.
The fry should be covered with a sieve and not a plate for 2-3 hours and then the fry stays crisp. If it is covered with a plate, they become soft.

ingredients.d: 400 g tender, peeled pieces of ridged gourd

recipes.name: Ridged Gourd Scrambled Eggs (Beerakaya Egg Bhurji)
recipes.note: A quick recipe that works well for bachelors and lunch boxes. Scrambled eggs need a lot of oil and should be fried well, then you get the taste.
steps: Heat oil and fry cumin seeds, green chillies, curry leaves, red chillies, and ginger.
Add chopped onion and fry till the raw smell is gone. Add ridged gourd pieces, add mirchi powder, turmeric, and salt, mix well. Cover it and cook on medium flame until oil separates.
When the oil separates, break the egg on the curry, and without stirring, cover it and let it cook on a medium flame for 3-4 minutes.
After three minutes, cut it into pieces with a ladle, mix it well and fry till the oil separates from the curry. It takes about 12-15 minutes for the curry to cook and oil to separate.
When the oil comes to the surface, add the chopped green coriander and garam masala and remove them from the fire.
It tastes excellent with rice, rotis as well as puris.

recipes.name: Katte Pongal (Ven Pongal)
recipes.note: Use dosa rice or ration rice rather than regular sona masoori rice, so the pongal stays soft even hours later. Add as much ghee as you can, it makes the pongal very tasty.
steps: Wash rice well and soak for 30 minutes.
Add green gram to a pan and roast on a low flame until it gives out an aroma. Then wash it.
If you are cooking separately, then take a thick-bottomed vessel, add 5 cups of water. Add salt, washed rice, washed green gram, and cook on a medium flame for 30 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Once the rice is cooked well, switch off the stove and set it aside.
If you cook pongal in the cooker, add all the ingredients, and cook up to 5 whistles and then add seasoning.
Melt ghee and add seasoning ingredients, fry well and mix in the pongal.

recipes.name: Curd Idly (Dahi Idli)
recipes.note: Made from leftover idlies. The curd should be thin and cool, dilute it with water, or the idly soaks up the water and turns like halwa.
steps: Add salt and sugar to cool, dilute curd and refrigerate for an hour.
Heat oil for seasoning and fry all the ingredients, and set aside.
If the idlies are cool, then sprinkle some water on them and then pour the curd mixture on them.
Then add the seasoning and the pomegranate seeds and serve. You could keep them in the fridge for an hour and then serve them too.

recipes.name: Tomato Dal (Tomato Pappu)
recipes.note: Wash and soak the dal for an hour before cooking. Cut the tomatoes into bigger pieces, smaller pieces become pulp during cooking.
steps: Cook soaked toor dal, Bengal gram, oil, turmeric, water and cook it till you get 2 whistles on high flame and 3 whistles on a low flame.
Mash the cooked dal properly.
Heat oil in a pan, add chopped onions, fry it for some time and add green chillies, salt, mirchi powder, and fry for some more time.
Now add tomato pieces, cook it for 3 minutes covering it with a lid.
Add sambar powder, tamarind pulp, and cook till the top layer of the tomatoes are cooked.
Add cooked dal to the mixture and cook it for 5 min adding sufficient water. Remove from fire.
Take oil and ghee for seasoning. Add mustard, Bengal gram, black gram, and other ingredients used for seasoning. Add it to the dal.
Add salt if required. It is best served with rice or chapati.
